featured.title: Going from AsyncWrite to AsyncRead

It's certainly an interesting abstraction. I was going to say that we could add one to tokio-util, and that you could ask the futures-util maintainers about that too. But:
Thinking a bit more about it, it does suffer one challenge, which is that when you stop reading, the internal future just stops running. featured.suggestedTitle: Exploring AsyncRead and AsyncWrite in Rust
featured.suggestedSummary: The Rust Internals forum is discussing the transition from AsyncWrite to AsyncRead, highlighting the challenges and potential solutions. The conversation centers on the utility of ReaderStream in conjunction with Axum, despite its dependency on Tokio. This exploration is crucial for Rust developers working with asynchronous I/O, as it delves into the intricacies of stream handling and the implications for efficient data processing in Rust applications.
featured.reason: Async I/O is crucial for Rust applications.

featured.title: Egui_tracing 0.3 — a live tracing/log viewer widget for egui apps
featured.summary:
Hi all,
I wanted to share egui_tracing, a small crate that gives any egui/eframe app an embedded log viewer. You register it as a tracing_subscriber layer once at startup, then drop a Logs widget anywhere in your UI and get filtering by level, filtering by target (with glob patterns), search, and a scrollable event list — both on native and wasm32.
It also bridges the log crate, so crates that haven't migrated to tracing still show up.

quickNews.title: [Pre-RFC] Bulk visibility syntax
quickNews.summary:
scottmcm:
Remember that extern "C" fn foo() { ... } and extern "C" { fn foo(); } are completely different.
Off topic, but I've wondered whether these could/should have been unified—whether unsafe extern "C" { fn foo(); } should have been spelled #[unsafe(no_mangle)] extern "C" fn foo();.
